argument: Twelve unequal cells must read as one compact body before they read as twelve controls. The apertures, overlap, seam hierarchy, and asymmetrical silhouette must carry the composition without interface chrome.

With labels, readout, controls, hint, and prose hidden, the first view must leave v046's vessel, v047's proof strip, and v048's reciprocal ecology. It should read as pressure-made topology, not a generic mosaic or dashboard.

The visitor must push, turn against resistance, and release. Pointer, touch, keyboard, and deterministic control paths must offer equivalent meaningful routes; no hover-only action may carry the work.

The provisional path remains geometry-neutral. Only sufficient pressure, opposition, resistance, and three turns can change the topology; a cursor trace or status message cannot substitute for produced form.
The pressure translation must alter cell coordinates, angle, scale, notch, apertures, and a produced join. Material is the topology engine, not an orange stroke over a fixed image.
Four folds must compound in one SVG body. Fold order must change the wrong pair, lift must reconstruct the exact prior topology, and release must return to the seeded quiet body.
Generated SVG paths, actual apertures, produced joins, and deterministic state are the medium. No screenshot, imported image, brush preset, or external font may carry the work.
p5.brush is translated from material production into pressure-as-belief. Brushes, watercolor, hatching, grain, source palette, source composition, source code, examples, and API surface are refused.

v049 changes representation, composition, encounter, temporal rule, shape vocabulary, and viewer task: SVG topology and counterpressure replace the Canvas ecology, proof strip, and vessel. Do not return to crowds, ledgers, or remote targets.

Delete v049 if any refused gesture commits, if only a local cell changes, if the join is cosmetic, if fold order is cosmetic, if later memory resets, if exact lifting fails, or if the blind body reads as a generic grid, mosaic, or interface.
